outcome_detail: Settled for $16.5 million CAD. Settlement agreement executed by all parties December 16, 2025; approved by the New Brunswick Court of King's Bench on March 12, 2026. Roughly $7.2 million remains for class members after legal fees and expenses; claims administered by KPMG with a filing deadline of April 13, 2027. Settlement followed a 2022 trial ruling and a 2023 Court of Appeal of New Brunswick decision holding the city vicariously liable, which the Supreme Court of Canada declined to review in 2024.
criminal_detail: Kenneth Estabrooks was convicted in 1999 of four counts of indecent assault and sentenced to six years in prison, where he died in 2005. He had earlier admitted in 1975 to sexual activity with two teenage boys, after which the police force transferred him to the city works department rather than prosecuting.
incident_date_approx: Abuse alleged from January 1, 1953 to November 1, 1975 (class period); Estabrooks also worked for the city works department until 1983
description: A class action was filed in 2013 against the City of Saint John on behalf of people sexually abused as children by Kenneth Estabrooks, a Saint John Police Force officer from the 1950s until 1975, when he was transferred to the city works department after admitting sexual misconduct involving two teenage boys. Estabrooks was convicted in 1999 of four counts of indecent assault, sentenced to six years, and died in prison in 2005; a private investigator retained by the city reported in 2013 that as many as 263 young people may have been abused. The action, with representative plaintiff Bobby Hayes, was certified in February 2017 and survived the city's appeals, including a 2019 Supreme Court of Canada refusal to block it. Courts ultimately held the city vicariously liable for Estabrooks's abuse while he was a police officer, and the Supreme Court of Canada declined the city's final appeal in 2024. A $16.5-million settlement executed on December 16, 2025 was approved by the Court of King's Bench on March 12, 2026, with class members able to file claims until April 13, 2027.
notes: Filed before 2021; included because resolution occurred in window (settlement approved March 2026). Class period covers abuse from 1953-1975; the certified class and settlement concern abuse by a single officer, treated as one consolidated record.

confidence_notes: All three seed titles recovered (the third seed title matched CBC's 'Saint John agrees to pay $16.5M' coverage of victims receiving compensation). Settlement_date recorded as the court-approval date (2026-03-12); the agreement itself was executed 2025-12-16. Reporting on the trial-level vicarious liability rulings is partly conflicting (a November 2022 ruling finding liability and a March 2023 decision reported as finding none, resolved by the Court of Appeal in 2023 and left standing by the SCC in 2024); the final legal position — city vicariously liable for abuse during his police service — is consistent across sources. Suit was originally reported as a $26M claim; settled at $16.5M.
